To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

insulin induces the activation and translocation into the nucleus of MEK and MAP kinases, and also activates CKII in the nucleus, which might be involved in the regulation of transcription factors and gene expression.
the insulin receptor activates nuclear serine/threonine kinases, which may regulate gene expression.
insulin activates nuclear kinase activities and stimulates the nuclear translocalization of MEK, which is a MAP kinase kinase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the insulin regulation of MAP kinases and other nuclear kinases and their potential role in the regulation by insulin of gene expression in the nucleus.
the regulation of the insulin signalling pathway by nuclear kinases.
the nuclear translocation and nuclear kinase activation induced by insulin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin activates MAP kinase in the cytoplamic compartment, which in turn translocates into the nucleus where it activates other nuclear kinases and/or phosphorylates nuclear substrates.
insulin signalling is mediated by a number of nuclear kinases, which are activated in the nucleus and/or translocated to the nucleus in response insulin.

the insulin-induced nuclear translocation of MEKK and MEK and the activation of nuclear MAP kinases and AP-1 binding activity are important events in the regulation of insulin-induced gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

insulin stimulates the activation of ser/thr protein kinases in the cytopl and the nucleus, and these activated kinases phosphorylate nuclear substrates that regulate gene transcription, including transcription factors.
insulin activates a number of serine/threonine kinases in a cell-specific manner, and that these kinases may regulate gene expression by phosphorylation of nuclear proteins.
insulin activates serine kinases, including CKII, MEK and MAP kinase, in the nucleus, and these kinases may play a role in the regulation by insulin of gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin stimulates a rapid activation of nuclear serine/threonine kinases, which might be involved in the regulation of transcriptional activity.
the MAP kinase cascade is not only activated in the cytoplams of cells in response to insulin but that the cascade is also activated in the nuclei of cells in response of insulin.
insulin stimulates the activation of nuclear kinases and the translocation of MEKS into the nucleus, and that these kinases are involved in the regulation of nuclear transcription.
